The location "medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella" is atypical for Osgood-Schlatter (which is anterior/tibial tuberosity) or patellar tendinitis (which is the tendon itself). This location is classic for medial patellofemoral pain or potentially a medial meniscus issue, but the lack of mechanical symptoms makes meniscus less likely. However, the description "medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella" could also refer to the medial collateral ligament (MCL) origin or pes anserine bursitis.
